I’ve been up and down for as long as I can remember, but the last few months have been… worse. There was this stretch—about two months—where I couldn’t seem to stop. I’d wake up at 3 a.m. with my mind racing, rearrange the shop display five times in one morning, take on a dozen commissions I didn’t have time for, and snap at my husband if he asked me to slow down. I even kissed someone at a wedding—totally out of nowhere, not like me at all. I felt wired, like I was buzzing under my skin, but when people pointed things out, I just got angry.

Then, just as fast, I crashed. For three months now, I can barely get out of bed. I sleep 12, 14 hours and still feel exhausted. The flowers at work all look gray. I can’t pick what to wear, what to eat—simple things paralyze me. Sometimes I stand on the balcony and feel this sudden urge to step forward, not because I’ve thought it through, just this… pull. But I don’t have a plan. I never act.

I’ve always been restless, but I don’t know if it’s always been this way or if it started with the mood swings. My thoughts race sometimes, but I can’t tell if that’s because I’m wired from stress—or something else.
D008-D001_h021.question_a:

I’d sleep 12, even 14 hours and still feel exhausted. I stopped enjoying arranging flowers, which has always been my passion—even spending time with my husband felt like a chore. I couldn’t make simple choices, like what to wear or what to make for dinner. Sometimes, these intense urges would hit me—like walking toward the edge of a bridge during a walk or stepping into traffic at a crosswalk—just sudden impulses with no plan, no intent, but so strong I had to grab onto something to stop myself.

Before that, though, there was this wild two-month stretch last fall where I was the opposite—I barely slept, maybe three or four hours, but I was wide awake, rearranging the entire shop at 2 a.m., texting clients about orders I hadn’t even discussed, starting six new floral projects at once. I was snappy over tiny things—like if a rose wasn’t the right shade, I’d snap at my assistant. And I had this fling with a supplier’s rep—completely out of character for me. Looking back, the hyperactivity, the racing thoughts, the impulsivity—it only happened during that time. I’ve never felt like that as a kid. It came on fast, out of nowhere.
